keyword: when is the rocket launch to the moon

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight to the moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; 'No other humans have traveled beyond lower Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in December 1972.' R2: 'first crewed mission to the moon in more than half a century. No other humans have traveled beyond lower Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in December 1972.' R5: 'first time in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm it as the first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit or to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission launched on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: Timestamps like '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026'; 'Wednesday evening'. R2: '1 Apr 2026'; 'Wednesday, April 1, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state launch on April 1, 2026, described as Wednesday.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.' R2: 'New time 6.35pm ET'; 'lifting off at 6.35pm'

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission launched from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the historic Launch Complex 39B.' R2: 'Kennedy Space Center.' R5: 'Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla.'

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission has a four-astronaut crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All sources list exactly four astronauts: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'about nine and a half days.' R2: '10-day lunar mission'; '10-day test flight.' R3: '10-day trip.' R4: '10-day journey.'
verifications.reasoning: Directly called 10-day in multiple sources; R1's 9.5 days is precise but aligns with common description.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission involves orbiting the moon before returning to Earth.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead, the plan is to loop around it.' R2: 'lunar flyby'; '10-day test flight, which will not land on the moon.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state no lunar orbit, only a flyby or loop around the moon.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket launched the Orion spacecraft.

verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm SLS launched Orion.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft carried astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All sources list exactly: Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names match across all sources.

verifications.reasoning: Immediate post-launch activities involve system checks.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission had a successful launch.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is a landing mission scheduled for the future.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R2: 'next moon landing scheduled for Artemis IV in 2028.' R4: 'beyond Artemis 3, at the moon.' R5: 'Artemis III... demonstrate... landing technologies in low-Earth orbit... moon landing... for Artemis IV.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources contradict: some imply Artemis III leads to moon but landing on IV; inconsistent attribution.
